paper_title: Thermal aware task assignment for multicore processors using genetic algorithm

extraction.paper_title: Thermal aware task assignment for multicore processors using genetic algorithm

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 5.3.2 and Figure 9 (non-equal initial temperature case), with the setup in Section 5.1 and Figure 6 and the task parameters in Table 1
scenario.description: Thermal-aware GA task assignment on a quad-core out-of-order processor. Task parameters come from gem5 and McPAT. HotSpot gives per-core temperatures over 10 hyper-periods. Initial core temperatures are 65.48, 49.77, 45.82 and 51.86 C with a 45 C ambient. Core temperature is rebalanced; the maximum inter-core difference is about 8 C after the first hyper-period (Figure 10).
scenario.architecture: Quad-core out-of-order CPU with 32 KB I-cache and D-cache, a dedicated 1 MB L2 per core, 64 MB RAM, a DDRx1 memory controller and a 2 GHz clock (Section 5.1, Figure 6). No block floorplan geometry is published.
scenario.workload: 20 independent periodic tasks from SPEC2006, MiBench and MediaBench (Table 1, PDF page 8), with per-task execution time, leakage power, dynamic power and energy.
scenario.operating_point: 2 GHz clock; ambient 45 C; initial core temperatures of 65.48, 49.77, 45.82 and 51.86 C; 10 hyper-periods (about 14 s of simulation, per the abstract and conclusion). The task power values in Table 1 are per task, not per block.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot thermal simulator (compact RC model) driven by gem5 execution times and McPAT task power; the per-core transient temperature is also described by a lumped RC model (Eqs. 1-2), PDF pages 3-7
original_setup.optimizer: Genetic algorithm (binary chromosome, one gene per task, tournament selection, single-point crossover, bitwise mutation, mu+lambda survivor selection) that assigns tasks to cores so each core's energy is about a_j times total energy (Eqs. 8-13, Algorithm-1), PDF pages 5-7
original_setup.controller: Temperature-driven task assignment per hyper-period under EDF scheduling: decision factors a_j are computed from the previous period's steady-state HotSpot core temperatures, with more energy given to cooler cores. This is not a DVFS or closed-loop continuous controller (PDF pages 5-7)
original_setup.benchmark: 20 tasks from SPEC2006, MiBench and MediaBench (Table 1, PDF page 8) on a quad-core out-of-order CPU at 2 GHz. Selected scenario: non-equal initial core temperatures (65.48, 49.77, 45.82, 51.86 C; ambient 45 C) over 10 hyper-periods (Section 5.3.2, Figure 9, PDF page 10)

thermal_observable.location: Maximum temperature difference between cores (inter-core spread) in each hyper-period, Figure 10 (PDF page 10). The paper states roughly 8 C, excluding the first hyper-period where the initial temperatures differ
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum inter-core temperature difference per hyper-period over 10 hyper-periods, about 14 s of simulation. The value is approximate and read from the text, not from a tabulated number

physical_mismatches.reason: No block floorplan is published. There are no x, y, width or height values for the cores, L2 caches or other blocks, and Figure 6 is an architecture diagram, not geometry. A steady 2D Studio floorplan therefore cannot be built from the paper without inventing geometry.

Table 1 gives per-task (benchmark) leakage and dynamic power, not per-block power for the same scenario. The paper does not publish a rule for mapping tasks to per-core block power, and the task-to-core assignment per hyper-period is only shown in figures. Total chip power cannot be split into per-block power without inventing a rule.

The original study is transient and scheduling-driven. It uses 10 hyper-periods of about 14 s with core temperatures feeding back into task assignment. A steady 2D thermal solve cannot reproduce the transient peaks or the assignment feedback loop.

The optimizer (GA task assignment) and controller (per-period thermal-aware scheduling under EDF) act on workload allocation, not on a floorplan or package parameters, so they have no counterpart in a static Studio steady-state solve.

The HotSpot package, cooling and material parameters (R and C values, heat sink, TIM, die thickness, ambient coupling beyond the 45 C ambient) are not reported, so the original thermal solver setup is not reproducible.

The system is a planar quad-core CPU with no 3D stacking, interposer or advanced cooling. These are not mismatches with a 2D Studio package, but they confirm that the paper's contribution is scheduling and not geometry.

methods.note: The text on PDF pages 3-7 and 10-11 supports the stated method: gem5 timing, McPAT power, a HotSpot-driven loop, a GA task assignment (Eqs. 8-13, Algorithm-1) and EDF scheduling. It also supports the claim that this is a transient scheduling study and not a steady 2D floorplan study. This is a text-only check. Figures 1-10 were not visually reviewed, so any method detail shown only in figures is unverified.

code.note: The packet assets list is empty. PDF pages 1-12 contain no repository, supplementary file or availability statement. No gem5, McPAT, HotSpot or GA code exists to check.

parameters.note: The GA parameters (Np, iter, k, rho_c, rho_m), the period and hyper-period lengths, and the HotSpot R, C and package values are not given. The extracted initial temperatures, 45 C ambient, 2 GHz clock and cache sizes match the paper text on pages 7 and 10. The KB/MB-to-byte conversions assume the binary convention, which the paper does not state. The decisive observable, about 8 C, appears only as approximate text ('slightly 8 C') and was not checked against Figure 10.

config.note: The experiment has an empty floorplan and empty power_w, so no complete scenario can be built. There are no block names, x/y/width/height values, HotSpot floorplan, package or material settings, or gem5/McPAT configuration files. Figure 6 is a diagram and was not visually verified. The kind custom_2d_steady also conflicts with the extraction's own steady_2d_relevant=false.

data.note: The Table 1 text on page 8 is plausible; spot checks of bzip2 and basicmath give energy equal to time times total power. It still gives per-task power only, with no same-scenario per-core or per-block power and no tabulated task-to-core assignment. The per-hyper-period temperatures in Figures 7-10 are not tabulated, no figure image was supplied, and no digitization or visual verification of the decisive Figure 9 or 10 exists. The paper's own text gives inconsistent spread values (8 C vs about 9 C).

findings.reason: The 8 C value is read from prose ('slightly 8 C'). Figure 10 and Figure 9, the decisive evidence, were not supplied as images or digitized, and the packet has no assets. The observable is not visually verified.

The paper contradicts itself on the spread. The abstract and conclusion say the highest inter-core difference is 8 C. Section 5.3.1 says nearly 9 C per hyper-period in the equal-temperature case. In the selected case the first hyper-period is excluded because the initial spread is about 19.7 C. So 8 C is not the highest difference over the run, and the extraction's observable definition needs this caveat.

The experiment is declared custom_2d_steady with floorplan=[] and power_w={}. There is no geometry or same-scenario per-block power, so the packet cannot be approved as a reproduction. The steady label also contradicts steady_2d_relevant=false and the transient, feedback-driven scheduling study.
No core or L2 block geometry is published, and Table 1 per-task power cannot be mapped to cores or blocks. A same-scenario power value for each floorplan block therefore does not exist.
The assets list is empty and no code, config or data link exists, so code, parameters and configuration cannot be verified.
The 32 KB, 1 MB and 64 MB entries use binary multipliers (1024, 1048576) that the paper does not specify. They are assumptions and not geometry, and they are irrelevant to the thermal setup.

basicmath and pgp sign/verify have identical rows (490.239 ms, 0.66866 W, 0.041022 W, 347.912 mJ). This may be a source duplication or an extraction error. It was not checked against a rendered table image.
The roughly 14 s duration for 10 hyper-periods is approximate. The hyper-period length and task periods are not stated, so the timeline cannot be reconstructed.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and the deterministic gate set simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false. Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped' because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power map. No Studio result exists, so there is no numerical comparison and no replication claim. The paper's selected scenario is the non-equal initial temperature case of thermal-aware GA task assignment on a quad-core out-of-order CPU (Section 5.3.2, Figure 9). The reported observable is an approximate maximum inter-core temperature difference of about 8 C per hyper-period, read from text and excluding the first hyper-period. It comes from a transient HotSpot study over 10 hyper-periods (about 14 s) with scheduling feedback, which is a different regime, aggregation (inter-core spread rather than peak or mean temperature) and boundary condition from any steady 2D run. A custom 2D steady run would also have no transient trace. The final verdict is that the scenario is not reproducible or comparable in Studio from the published information. Qualitatively, the paper's finding is that temperature-driven workload allocation reduces core-to-core thermal imbalance. A static floorplan solve cannot test that mechanism, because the optimizer and controller act on task assignment, not on geometry or package parameters. The evidence validation also flagged that no evidence items have a valid page or pinned asset locator, there is no cited steady or transient regime for the observable, and the adversarial and independent reviews were unresolved or not approved. No external artifacts were found (checked_no_links), so the claims are unverified against code or data.
limitations: Studio was not run; there is no simulated output, so no numerical comparison to the reported ~8 C inter-core spread is possible or valid.
Mismatch: no block floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) for cores, L2 caches or other blocks is published, so a 2D layout would have to be invented.
Mismatch: Table 1 gives per-task leakage and dynamic power, not per-block power, and no mapping rule or tabulated per-hyper-period task-to-core assignment is published.
Mismatch in regime: the original study is transient (10 hyper-periods, about 14 s) with thermal feedback into task assignment, whereas a custom 2D run would be steady with no transient trace.

Mismatch in observable and aggregation: the paper's ~8 C is an approximate maximum inter-core difference per hyper-period read from text, excluding the first hyper-period; it is not a peak, mean or steady-state temperature at a defined location.
Mismatch in boundary and package assumptions: only a 45 C ambient is reported; HotSpot package, heat sink, TIM, die thickness, material properties and R/C values are missing.
The GA optimizer and per-period EDF thermal-aware scheduling controller have no counterpart in a static Studio solve.
